method: Visual inspection of six predetermined frames at 20%, 50%, and 80% of both fully verified final replays; post-hoc analysis of contiguous upright samples in the saved phase-zero traces.
summary: Both sampled final policies retain knee-scooting: low pelvis, a folded leg near the track, and the opposite leg extended forward. The gait reward changes geometric proxies but the reviewed samples do not show convincing upright running.
decision: Do not promote this reward as an upright-running solution. Retain both models and all intermediate outcomes.
limits: One paired training seed, two familiar reset phases, geometric knee proximity rather than contact measurements, and sampled visual review rather than a claim about every instant.
